annotations.title: Bed, Ways, and Pedestal Base
annotations.overview: The bed is the long foundation of the lathe, with precision ways along its top and a pedestal base below.
annotations.function: It keeps the headstock, carriage, and tailstock aligned while carrying cutting forces and the machine’s weight.
annotations.relationships: The carriage and tailstock travel on the ways, while the headstock is fixed at one end of the bed.
annotations.inspection: Observe the bed ways for clean, continuous bearing surfaces, damaged edges, trapped swarf, or obstacles in the carriage path.
annotations.safety: Keep hands and clothing away from moving carriage travel. Report damaged ways or loose foundation hardware before operating the lathe.

evidence.title: 29 CFR 1910.212 General requirements for all machines

annotations.title: Headstock and Drive System
annotations.overview: The headstock is the fixed housing at the operating end of the lathe, containing the spindle drive and speed-changing mechanism.
annotations.function: It supplies controlled rotary motion to the spindle so a secured workpiece can turn for facing, turning, drilling, or threading.
annotations.relationships: Its spindle projects toward the carriage and tailstock, and its controls coordinate with the feed and threading mechanisms.
annotations.inspection: Check the headstock housing for secure covers, readable controls, unusual vibration signs, and clear space around drive openings before use.
annotations.safety: Never reach near a rotating spindle or open drive cover. Stop the machine before investigating an unfamiliar sound or vibration.

evidence.title: 29 CFR 1910.212 General requirements for all machines

annotations.title: Spindle, Chuck, and Workpiece
annotations.overview: The spindle carries the chuck, which grips the long coaxial demonstration workpiece shown here; it is not a permanent machine component.
annotations.function: Together, the spindle and chuck rotate a properly secured workpiece so a stationary cutting tool can remove material.
annotations.relationships: The chuck mounts at the headstock spindle nose, faces the tool post, and may be supported at the far end by the tailstock.
annotations.inspection: Before operation, confirm the chuck jaws visibly contact the workpiece, the key is removed, and no projecting stock can strike nearby equipment.
annotations.safety: Treat the rotating chuck and workpiece as entanglement and impact hazards. Stand clear during startup and never touch them while they move.

evidence.title: 29 CFR 1910.212 General requirements for all machines

annotations.title: Speed and Feed Selector Controls
annotations.overview: These levers and selectors choose spindle-speed ranges and feed settings on a conventional lathe before cutting begins.
annotations.function: They route motion through the headstock and gearbox so spindle rotation and tool travel match the material and intended operation.
annotations.relationships: The controls affect the headstock drive, feed rod, lead screw, carriage apron, and threading arrangement rather than cutting independently.
annotations.inspection: Read each selector marking and look for missing knobs, bent levers, unclear positions, or signs that a control does not seat positively.
annotations.safety: Change settings only with the machine stopped unless its instructions specifically say otherwise. Avoid reaching across a rotating chuck to use controls.

evidence.title: 29 CFR 1910.212 General requirements for all machines

annotations.title: Chuck Safety Guard
annotations.overview: The chuck safety guard is a transparent barrier positioned between the operator and the rotating chuck and workholding area.
annotations.function: It helps reduce exposure to thrown chips, coolant splash, and accidental contact with rotating parts while preserving a view of the cut.
annotations.relationships: The guard works with the chuck, workpiece, and operator position; it does not replace correct workholding or safe setup practices.
annotations.inspection: Look for a complete guard panel, sound hinges or mountings, clear viewing area, and a position that covers the chuck’s likely danger zone.
annotations.safety: Use the guard as intended and do not defeat an interlock. A guard cannot make loose clothing, gloves, or an unsecured workpiece safe.

evidence.title: 29 CFR 1910.212 General requirements for all machines

annotations.title: Carriage and Apron Assembly
annotations.overview: The carriage is the moving platform that carries the cutting tool along the bed; the apron is its front control housing.
annotations.function: It provides hand or powered longitudinal and cross movement, placing the tool accurately relative to the rotating workpiece.
annotations.relationships: The carriage rides on the bed ways, supports the compound rest, and receives drive through the feed rod or lead screw.
annotations.inspection: Observe the carriage saddle, apron controls, handwheel, and travel path for trapped chips, visible damage, or contact with the guard or tailstock.
annotations.safety: Keep fingers away from the bed ways and carriage pinch points. Stop motion before clearing swarf or checking anything near the apron.

evidence.title: 29 CFR 1910.212 General requirements for all machines

annotations.title: Compound Rest and Tool Post
annotations.overview: The compound rest sits on the carriage and carries the tool post, giving the cutting tool a short, adjustable angled slide.
annotations.function: It holds and positions a tool holder for fine feeding, facing, turning, and angled cuts such as short chamfers.
annotations.relationships: It is mounted above the carriage cross slide and faces the spindle-held workpiece, with the tool post clamping the selected tool.
annotations.inspection: Check the compound slide, tool-post clamp, tool-holder seating, and exposed tool overhang for obvious looseness, damage, or interference with the chuck.
annotations.safety: Keep the cutting edge below the workpiece centerline only when the approved setup calls for it. Never adjust the tool post during rotation.

evidence.title: 29 CFR 1910.212 General requirements for all machines

annotations.title: Half-Nut and Feed Controls
annotations.overview: The half-nut and feed controls on the apron engage either carriage feed or the lead screw for controlled threading motion.
annotations.function: The half-nut closes around the lead screw to synchronize carriage travel with spindle rotation when cutting a thread.
annotations.relationships: These controls connect the apron to the lead screw and feed rod, working with the headstock selector settings and carriage.
annotations.inspection: Identify the half-nut lever and feed controls, then check their labels, free movement, and clearance from the rotating workpiece and chuck.
annotations.safety: Engage threading controls only with a planned setup and safe position. Do not place hands near the lead screw while the lathe runs.

evidence.title: 29 CFR 1910.212 General requirements for all machines

annotations.title: Tailstock Assembly
annotations.overview: The tailstock is the movable support at the far end of the bed, opposite the headstock and spindle.
annotations.function: It supports long work with a center or holds a drill in line with the workpiece axis for axial operations.
annotations.relationships: The tailstock slides on the same bed ways as the carriage and aligns with the spindle centerline and demonstration workpiece.
annotations.inspection: Observe the tailstock base, clamp area, body alignment, and clearance to the carriage; note chips that could prevent full seating.
annotations.safety: Secure the tailstock before applying cutting load. Keep clear of the center and any rotating workpiece while the spindle is running.

evidence.title: 29 CFR 1910.212 General requirements for all machines

annotations.title: Tailstock Quill and Handwheel
annotations.overview: The tailstock quill is the extendable sleeve within the tailstock, advanced and retracted by its handwheel.
annotations.function: It brings a center, drill, or other approved shank tool toward the workpiece while preserving alignment with the spindle axis.
annotations.relationships: The quill is part of the tailstock assembly and approaches the workpiece held by the chuck, usually opposite the headstock.
annotations.inspection: Check the quill’s visible surface, handwheel, locking control, and tool opening for chips, scoring, or anything that could obstruct smooth travel.
annotations.safety: Retract and secure the quill before moving the tailstock. Do not hold a tool or center by hand against a rotating workpiece.

evidence.title: 29 CFR 1910.212 General requirements for all machines

annotations.title: Steady Rest
annotations.overview: The steady rest is a fixed support that surrounds part of a long workpiece between the headstock and tailstock.
annotations.function: Its adjustable contact points help resist deflection and vibration when a long, slender workpiece needs support away from its ends.
annotations.relationships: It mounts to the bed ways and supports the rotating workpiece while remaining clear of the carriage, tool, and chuck.
annotations.inspection: Check that the steady rest sits flat on the bed, its contact points are present, and its opening is clear of chips before setup.
annotations.safety: A steady rest must be aligned and secured before rotation. Keep hands away from its contact area and the turning workpiece.

evidence.title: 29 CFR 1910.212 General requirements for all machines

annotations.title: Work Light Assembly
annotations.overview: The work light assembly directs supplemental light toward the cutting area so the operator can better see the tool and workpiece.
annotations.function: It improves visibility for observation of setup and cutting conditions; it does not make close approach to moving machinery safe.
annotations.relationships: The light is mounted near the work zone and illuminates the chuck, tool post, carriage, and the exposed portion of the workpiece.
annotations.inspection: Check the work light head, support arm, power lead, lens condition, and position to ensure it does not obstruct guards or operator movement.
annotations.safety: Keep the work light outside the rotating envelope and away from coolant spray where required. Replace damaged electrical equipment through approved channels.

evidence.title: 29 CFR 1910.212 General requirements for all machines

annotations.title: Coolant Delivery Nozzle
annotations.overview: The coolant delivery nozzle is the adjustable outlet that aims cutting fluid toward the tool-workpiece contact area.
annotations.function: It directs coolant or lubricant to help manage heat, chip flow, and cutting conditions during appropriate machining operations.
annotations.relationships: The nozzle serves the tool post and rotating workpiece area, while its hose connects it to the lathe’s coolant supply.
annotations.inspection: Check the nozzle tip, flexible hose, mounting point, and aim for leaks, damage, and adequate clearance from the chuck and workpiece.
annotations.safety: Aim coolant before starting and keep the nozzle outside rotating reach. Avoid splashing floors or electrical parts, and follow site fluid practices.
